sections.label: ✨ Improve
items: Sorting one sub-section on a multi-table page (artist discographies, release-group release lists, relationship pages, …) now rebuilds only that sub-table. Previously every sub-table on the page was torn down and re-created to re-order one — 124 rows across 3 sub-tables to sort a single 119-row one, or all 123 rows across 17 sections on an artist page.

Technical: the sort handler mutates exactly one `groupedRows[i].rows` array, then called `_invalidateFilterCache(); runFilter();`. The wholesale cache clear forced a full `testRowMatch()` membership pass over every row of every group even though a re-order cannot change which rows match, and `runFilter()` then re-cloned, re-stripped, re-highlighted and re-inserted all of them. New `_renderDirtyGroupIdxs` names the groups a sort actually disturbed; `runFilter()`'s multi branch skips the clone/strip/highlight pass for the rest, and `renderGroupedTable()`'s reuse branch leaves their `<tbody>` — and their whole per-group decorate pass, including `initCollapsableColumns()`'s full unique-value column scan — untouched.

New `_invalidateFilterCacheForGroups()` drops only the disturbed groups' cached match sets, and does so across ALL `discographyViewState` values rather than just the current one: the multi cache key is `m:<view>:<groupIdx>`, so keying on the current view alone would leave a pre-sort ordering cached under another view, ready to be resurrected on the next switch. Single-table sorts keep the wholesale invalidation — `allRows` is one array under one key, so there is nothing to narrow.

Merged discography view is the deliberate carve-out. It renders a category from the union of every same-category group, re-sorted through `mergedSortComparatorRegistry`, so `_sortDirtyGroupIdxs()` adds those co-contributors to the dirty set. Verified they cost nothing: they are the hidden duplicate tables whose rows are already folded into the visible one, so re-rendering them empties their `<tbody>` and inserts no rows at all — measured, not assumed.

The colon-alignment finalizers (`finalizeSplitAlignedColumns`/`finalizeRLCColumnWidths`) are skipped on a scoped pass. They measure one shared column width across the whole rendered row set, which a re-order does not change; running them against a `filteredArray` with the undisturbed groups emptied would have narrowed every column to what the sorted sub-table alone needs.

Measured: rows re-inserted by a sort went from 7 to 6 on the small pilot release group and from 124 to 119 on a 124-row/3-sub-table one. On the shape this is actually for — a 123-row artist discography across 17 sub-sections, sorting a 61-row one — 123 re-insertions became 61 and the sort went from a 114 ms median to 83 ms (3 runs each, same page, same section, toggled in place). Artwork is unaffected: icons and inline thumbnails still arrive already painted, and the sort still issues zero requests to the archive.

Side effect, found while checking why a saved file grew: the 📊 unique-value count badges and their tooltips now SURVIVE a sort of an unrelated sub-section instead of blanking back to a placeholder and being recomputed. `initCollapsableColumns()`'s per-column scan is part of the per-group work that is now skipped for an undisturbed table, and its counts were still correct — a sort changes a group's row ORDER, never its row set. Measured on a saved payload: 19 of 22 badges populated afterwards, against 0 of 22 before.
